newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds relax at end of rewarding week.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds relax at end of rewarding week.

text.p: *Australian bonds finish a fairly busy week on a quiet note, market having been basically square after Thursday's rally.
*Next major local influence seen as Q1 CPI data on April 23, although weak housing finance data on Monday could be positive.
Australian bonds took the opportunity for a quiet Friday after a week that saw the yield on 10-year bonds move back under 8.00 percent and spreads to U.S. Treasuries come in to two month lows.
"It was pretty quiet," one trader said. "There was a bit of buying into 9.30 this morning (when rate changes are announced), and once that was out of the way, a bit of squaring up."
But even squaring activity was limited, with many players having squared up for today's U.S. March retail trade and producer price data after Thursday's rally on weak employment data, traders said.
The tender of A$300 million of Treasury adjustable rate bonds, which went a a weighted average of 15.07 points under the bank bill swap rate, had little market impact, traders said.

While the market will take some direction from today's U.S. data and next week's U.S. inflation figures (CPI), bonds are expected to remain supported ahead of what are expected to be favourable first quarter inflation data on April 23.

That tone is likely to be supported by February housing finance data on Monday. Economists expect it to show a fall of 8.0 percent, a result that would add to some emerging doubts over the robustness of the economy.

Spreads continue to narrow against Canada and the U.S. on Friday, and are narrower across the board over the week. Spread to U.S. 10-years is at its narrowest since mid-February. Potential for curve to steepen further if short end factors out 1997 rate hike.
